A nil response gives err direct_no_response, and a non-map response gives direct_invalid. The function's own failure channel: direct is not declared `throws`, so it never throws and never uses a second return value. A denied allow.op also comes back as ok false plus err.

differences: remove and data: swift replaces the entity's data with the remove response body when that body is non-nil (EntityRemoveOp.fragment.swift:18). cpp keeps data_ unchanged (EntityRemoveOp.fragment.cpp:12-18).

remove and the deleted mark: swift marks deleted only when result.ok (EntityBase.fragment.swift:167-169). cpp calls markDeleted() unconditionally after runOp, so with ctrl throw:false a failed remove is still marked deleted (EntityRemoveOp.fragment.cpp:25).

A failed op with throw:false: swift returns the error fallback Value (result.resdata) instead of the entity (EntityBase.fragment.swift:174). cpp load and remove always return self() (EntityLoadOp.fragment.cpp:28).

stream signal: swift reads callopts.signal as a native () -> Bool and stops yielding when it returns true, though the check happens while stream() is still building the AsyncStream. cpp has no signal at all.
stream return type: swift returns AsyncStream<Value>; cpp returns a std::vector<Value>. Both run the operation at the call.
direct err: swift's err is .nat(ProjectNameError), an error object with a code. cpp's err is a plain map {"message": string} with no code.
direct's failure channel: swift's direct is non-throwing by signature. cpp's direct catches only SdkErrorPtr, so other exceptions can escape.
Live transport: swift ships a URLSession transport (Fetcher.swift:89). cpp ships none and throws fetch_no_transport without options.system.fetch (pipeline.hpp:608-613).

Entity member access: in swift, name, client, data, match and entopts are internal, so a program reaches them only through getName(), data(), matchv() and deleted(). In cpp they are public fields (name_, client, data_, match_, deleted_, entopts) that hold the live values, and the client's options and utility are public fields too.
Match getter name: swift matchv(); cpp match().
Accessor naming: swift uses the PascalCase entity name (client.Planet()); cpp uses a lower snake-case name (client->planet(), graph_ql()).
Construction failure on a missing server variable: swift traps with fatalError (MakeOptions.swift:148); cpp throws an SdkErrorPtr server_var_required from the constructor (pipeline.hpp:1936).
surprises: cpp has no built-in HTTP transport. Every live call fails with fetch_no_transport unless options.system.fetch holds a callable (tm/cpp/utility/pipeline.hpp:610-613), and no old page says so.

Model B's base URL is templated with server variables, but the swift and cpp quick starts (root and per-language) pass none, so they fail at construction: swift with fatalError, cpp with server_var_required.

Swift's stream comment says the signal is 'honoured between yields', but the loop runs inside the AsyncStream build closure, which Swift runs during construction, so the check happens before the caller iterates.

answers.answer: The result is a struct `value` Map. (a) 2xx: `ok` = `Bool true`, plus `status` (Num), `headers` and `data`; no err. (b) Non-2xx with a readable body: `ok` = `Bool false`, `status`, `headers`, `data` holding the error body; no `err`. (c) Unreadable body: `ok` = `Bool false`, `status`, `headers`, `data` Noval, and `err`, a cleaned `{code, message}` map. This happens even for 2xx. (d) The request cannot be made: `{ok: Bool false, err}` only. NOTE that without `options.system.fetch` or the test feature, EVERY live request is case (d). The runtime bundles no HTTP transport, and the fetcher returns `fetch_no_transport`. A prepare failure, a mode or test block, and a nil or non-map response are also case (d). A denied op gives `err` as a `Str`. Failure channel: direct catches `Sdk_error_exc` from prepare and returns the map. It does not catch other OCaml exceptions, such as one raised inside a caller's system.fetch `Func`; those propagate.

differences: Utility on the entity: clojure's `:_utility` is a COPY (get-utility makes a new atom, Entity.fragment.clj:34). OCaml's `e_utility` IS the client's utility record (Entity_ocaml.ts:63,69).

Options and utility getters: clojure has `options-map` (clone) in sdk.api, and `get-utility` (shallow copy) only in sdk.client. OCaml has no getter in Sdk_client, only the live fields `cl_options`/`cl_utility`, plus the clone helper Sdk_helpers.client_options_map.

The deleted mark: clojure sets `:_deleted` only on success (`(if (= out ent) (mark-deleted ent) out)`, frag:248). OCaml sets `e_deleted` unconditionally after run_op returns (EntityOperation_ocaml.ts:265-267), so with throw:false a failed remove still reads as deleted.
Op result with throw:false: a clojure op returns the bare failure value when the pipeline failed (op-return, frag:65-67). OCaml returns the entity regardless (EntityOperation_ocaml.ts:269-270).

Test constructor without the test feature: clojure still gets the full mock, because features.clj is untrimmed (trim: false). OCaml's factory falls back to base_feature, and every request fails with fetch_mode_block.
Live transport: clojure ships java.net.http (core.clj:1873). OCaml ships NONE: without system.fetch, every live request fails with fetch_no_transport (sdk_runtime.ml:1573-1579).

Form: clojure entities are maps with the ops as namespace functions `(e-x/load ent m ctrl)`, and the deleted mark is a namespace fn over an atom. OCaml entities are records with the ops as closure fields `ent.e_load m ctrl`, and `e_deleted` is a plain bool field.
Signal type: clojure takes a plain Clojure 0-arg fn, true-ish to stop. OCaml takes a struct `Func` value that must return `Bool true`.
direct `err` value: clojure gives an SDK error Clojure map with keyword keys (:code :msg ...). OCaml gives a struct Map `{code, message}`. Both give a string for allow.op denial.
Packaging: clojure has deps.edn with :paths ["src"], so a program only needs the classpath. OCaml has no library artifact, so a program must compile all SDK sources in a fixed order.
surprises: OCaml bundles no HTTP transport at all. A live OCaml client cannot make a request unless the caller passes options.system.fetch. No old page says so, and the README's live quick start and 'Run live tests' imply otherwise.
In both languages the accessor's argument is entity OPTIONS, not data, although the clojure REFERENCE calls it 'initial data'.
Both streams are lazy in name only: the request and every item are fetched before the sequence is returned, and only the signal check is deferred.
In both languages a remove REPLACES the entity's data with the response's data, despite the code comments (and the ocaml page) saying it keeps the data it held.
The old clojure and ocaml READMEs both have TypeScript code blocks in their 'Error handling' sections (and clojure in 'Entity state').
clojure's documented `(api/get-utility client)` does not exist in sdk.api.
